name: Little Otter
one_liner: Video therapy, parent coaching and psychiatry for children 0–18 and their parents, starting with a whole-family mental health check-up.
best_for: Parents of young children (including toddlers) with behavior, anxiety or mood concerns
Families who want the child's therapy and parent support coordinated in one place
Families with in-network coverage through BCBS, Florida Blue or Kaiser Northern California in served states
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Families who rely on Medicaid or Tricare
Children who need in-person, intensive or inpatient care
Families outside the states it serves
short_description: Virtual family mental health care for kids 0–18 and parents: therapy, parent coaching and psychiatry; some insurance, or $200/session self-pay.
long_description: Little Otter is a virtual mental health service built around the whole family. Care starts with a family mental health check-up and an assessment, then a care plan that can include therapy for the child, parent coaching, couples or parent therapy, and psychiatry with medication management. It treats children from birth to 18, including anxiety, depression, ADHD, behavior and trauma, as well as parents' and perinatal mental health. Self-pay prices are $350 for the assessment, $200 per therapy or parent coaching session and $250 per psychiatry session, with bundle discounts but no sliding scale. It is in-network with plans including Independence Blue Cross, AmeriHealth NJ, Florida Blue, Kaiser Northern California and BCBS of Minnesota and North Carolina, and provides superbills for out-of-network claims; it does not take Medicaid or Tricare. Its outcome figures come from company reports; no peer-reviewed study of its care was found.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance in some states; $200/session self-pay therapy ($350 assessment)
pricing.notes: Self-pay: assessment $350, therapy $200/session, parent coaching $200/session, psychiatry $250/session; first matching appointment free; bundle discounts, no sliding scale or payment plans. In-network with Independence Blue Cross, AmeriHealth (NJ), Sana, Florida Blue, Kaiser Northern California, BCBS Minnesota and BCBS North Carolina; superbills for out-of-network. Not covered by Medicaid or Tricare. Therapy is HSA/FSA eligible.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell or share personal information for cross-context advertising, though its sites use analytics and ad-tech cookies; health records are handled under HIPAA as a business associate of its affiliated medical practices.

seo.meta_description: Little Otter provides virtual mental health care for children ages 0-14 and their families, with therapy, psychiatry, and parent coaching.

faqs.q: What ages does Little Otter serve?
faqs.a: Little Otter serves children from birth through 14 years old. Services are tailored to developmental stage—infant/toddler care focuses heavily on parent coaching, while older children receive more direct therapy. The family-centered model applies across all ages.

Little Otter accepts some insurance plans and partners with employers to provide covered mental health benefits. Coverage varies by plan and location. Contact them to verify if your insurance or employer benefit includes Little Otter.

faqs.q: What is parent coaching at Little Otter?
faqs.a: Parent coaching helps caregivers learn strategies to support their child's mental health at home. Since children spend most time with family, parent coaching extends treatment beyond therapy sessions. It's included as part of the family-centered care model.

faqs.q: Can Little Otter prescribe ADHD medication?
faqs.a: Yes, Little Otter offers child psychiatry for medication management including ADHD medications when appropriate. Psychiatric evaluation and ongoing medication management happen via video appointments with child psychiatrists.

patient_summary: You start with a free family mental health check-up and a free matching call, then your child, you, or both see a Little Otter clinician by video for therapy, parent coaching or psychiatry. It is in-network with some insurers in some states; otherwise you pay $350 for the assessment and $200 per therapy session.
